questions.q: What problem did Chapter 3's finale flag that Unity Catalog addresses?
options: Nothing controlled who could query or modify bronze.trips, silver.trips, or gold.daily_revenue — any workspace user could read or write any of them
The pipeline's tasks weren't chained correctly
Delta tables couldn't be queried with SQL
The medallion pipeline lacked a quarantine table
questions.explain: Unity Catalog is Databricks' governance layer sitting on top of every table already built, without changing how the code works.

questions.q: What is a metastore in Unity Catalog's object hierarchy?
options: The top-level container, scoped to one cloud region, typically shared across multiple workspaces in that region
A synonym for a single Delta table
The lowest-level object, below tables and views
A feature only available in the Standard pricing tier
questions.explain: A permission granted once at the metastore level applies everywhere that metastore is attached.

questions.q: How do catalogs, schemas, and tables relate to each other in the hierarchy?
options: Catalogs organize data at the highest level within a metastore; each catalog holds schemas; each schema holds tables, views, volumes, and other objects
Tables contain catalogs, which contain schemas
Schemas and catalogs are the same thing, just different names
Catalogs only exist within tables, not the other way around
questions.explain: This sets up Lesson 39's three-level namespace: catalog.schema.table.

questions.q: Why does attaching one metastore to multiple workspaces matter?
options: A permission granted once applies everywhere that metastore is attached, rather than needing to be set per-workspace with no shared source of truth
It has no real effect on how permissions work
Each workspace still needs its own completely separate set of permissions regardless
It only affects billing, not governance
questions.explain: Before Unity Catalog, permissions were often set per-workspace with no shared source of truth.

questions.q: Does adopting Unity Catalog require rewriting the PySpark/SQL code from Chapters 1-3?
options: No — everything from Chapters 1-3 keeps working exactly as written; Unity Catalog adds a governance layer on top
Yes, every DataFrame operation must be rewritten to use a new API
Yes, but only the write operations need to change
Only streaming pipelines need to be rewritten
questions.explain: This chapter adds governance concepts layered on top, not a rewrite of anything already built.
